hints.title: Project-Specific Seniority Ranking
hints.text: Identify the employee or employees possessing the highest tenure in years within each individual project.

hints.title: Dense Rank Window Partition
hints.text: Assign a dense ranking partitioned by project identifier and ordered descending by experience years, filtering for rank one.

hints.title: Project Experience Query Blueprint
hints.text: with Ranked as (select p.project_id, p.employee_id, dense_rank() over (partition by p.project_id order by e.experience_years desc) as rnk from Project p join Employee e on p.employee_id = e.employee_id) select project_id, employee_id from Ranked where rnk = 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT p.project_id, p.employee_id,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.project_id ORDER BY e.experience_years DESC) AS rnk
    FROM Project p
    JOIN Employee e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
)
SELECT project_id, employee_id
FROM Ranked
WHERE rnk = 1;
```

variables: P: total number of project assignments
complexity.notes: Joining tables followed by window partitioning and ranking executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated max subqueries on unindexed tables perform repeated full table scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking computes group maximums in a single scan without subquery re-execution.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of DENSE_RANK() or RANK() window functions partitioned by project.

import pandas as pd

def project_employees_iii(project: pd.DataFrame, employee: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = project.merge(employee, on='employee_id')
    max_exp = df.groupby('project_id')['experience_years'].transform('max')
    res = df[df['experience_years'] == max_exp]
    return res[['project_id', 'employee_id']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Merge and Groupby Transform Max Filter
